core.title: Keep every plan artifact valid against the schema shipped for its kind
core.given: A recognized plan artifact (a kind listed by the profile) outside the never-scanned vendored/generated trees — new, edited or already present
core.when: The planner authors or edits plan artifacts, or plan validation runs over the repository
core.then: Every such artifact satisfies the schema shipped for its kind.
prefer: Correct the field the finding names, as the schema requires.
Check the schema shipped for the artifact's kind before adding or renaming fields.
avoid: Leaving a schema violation in place on the assumption that downstream rules will tolerate it — they assume the schema shape and break silently.
Editing or loosening the shipped schema to make an artifact pass.
unless: Vendored and generated trees are never scanned — exactly the trees fixed by this check's own exclusion classification (see verification), not the stack-wide never-scanned union.
core.why: The schemas are the shape every other rule assumes. An artifact that breaks its schema breaks those assumptions silently.
evidence: The schema validation check, run over all recognized plan artifacts in the repository (not only changed ones), reports no schema violations — neither under this catch-all rule nor under the canonical rule a violation is routed to.
Each finding is fixed by correcting the named field as the schema requires.
verification: Validate every recognized plan artifact against the schema shipped for its kind, regardless of whether it changed.

Routing decides attribution only: a violation that belongs to a canonical rule is reported under that rule; every other violation is reported under this rule (catch-all). Either way the artifact is still required to conform.

Never scan vendored and generated trees. The exact exclusion classification is owned by this check and fixed in the realization's verification, not taken from the stack-wide never-scanned union (profile:roots.excluded): the union's additional entries are not silently inherited by this rule, and the check's exact fixed list is this rule's complete exclusion boundary — no discretionary further exclusions, so every recognized plan artifact outside that exact list is validated.
Schema validation operates on a parsed document, so parsing runs first; a parse failure is not an exemption from schema conformity — the artifact must both parse and conform.
Severity 3; strict disposition: fails on every finding, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

fires: A planner creates or edits a plan artifact of any recognized kind (including a plan artifact with its acceptances).
Plan validation runs over a repository containing existing, unchanged recognized plan artifacts.
A recognized plan artifact fails its schema, including violations that are reported under a canonical rule.
doesNotFire: Files inside the vendored/generated trees this check never scans (its exact, realization-fixed classification).
Files that are not a recognized plan artifact kind.

The stack's single, stack-wide union of never-scanned vendored and generated trees, exactly as the vocabulary defines it (in ATDD-Bun the union also includes version-control and repository-configured excludes). It is stack-wide scan context only, not this rule's boundary: this check owns the exact classification of the trees it never scans, fixed in its realization (kept in bunOnly), so the union's additional entries are not silently inherited by this rule.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the enforcing package ships the schemas that define each recognized plan artifact kind's format — the location the planner consults before adding or renaming fields and the location the check validates against (one schema per kind). Locations only, per the key's documented meaning; the schema technology itself is a realization detail (see bunOnly on then and verifier_detail[0]).

bunOnly.text: Every such artifact satisfies its JSON Schema in `planner-schemas/`.
bunOnly.reason: Split per the audit: the schema location (`planner-schemas/`) is profile data under layout.schemas#schema_location, whose documented meaning covers locations only. The schema technology — JSON Schema — is this realization's way of expressing artifact-format schemas; no v3 vocabulary key's documented meaning covers a schema-technology or validation idiom, and this round's findings are fixed without proposing new keys, so the exact technology stays per-realization here. The neutral core refers to 'the schema shipped for its kind', and instantiating the Bun realization adds the JSON Schema requirement back from this entry.

bunOnly.text: Vendored and generated trees (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`) are never scanned.
bunOnly.reason: This check's checker-owned exact exclusion classification, fixed by the realization to exactly these four trees; it is deliberately narrower than the stack-wide never-scanned union (profile:roots.excluded also covers version-control and repository-configured excludes). The neutral exception and the checker-ownership are kept in core:unless[0] and core:verification; the exact trees stay here so the authoritative Bun scope is preserved without silently inheriting additional union exclusions.

bunOnly.reason: Names this realization's validator id and rule id; the neutral equivalent (a schema validation check reported under this catch-all rule or the canonical rule it routes to) is kept in core:evidence[0].

bunOnly.reason: Same split as then: the schema location is profile data (layout.schemas#schema_location); the concrete schema technology — JSON Schema documents interpreted by this realization's validator — has no covering vocabulary key and no new key is proposed this round, so it is retained here and restored when instantiating the Bun realization. core:verification states the check generically as validating against 'the schema shipped for its kind'.

neutralityNotes: The plan-artifact kind taxonomy is profile data (roles.plan_artifact.kinds), and the shipped-schema reference is split per the audit: the schema location is profile data under layout.schemas#schema_location, restricted to locations exactly as the key's documented meaning defines (bunValue `planner-schemas/`), while the schema technology itself — JSON Schema — has no covering key in the closed v3 vocabulary (layout.schemas covers locations, and no idiom key's documented meaning covers an artifact-schema validation idiom); since this round's findings are fixed without proposing new keys, the technology is kept as a realization detail in bunOnly (on then and verifier_detail[0]) and restored when instantiating the Bun realization. The core therefore names no path, directory, schema technology or tool. Per the vocabulary, roots.excluded is preserved strictly as the stack-wide never-scanned union (which in ATDD-Bun also includes version-control and repository-configured excludes); this check owns the exact classification of the trees it never scans, which is stated in core:verification and fixed per realization — the reference realization's exact four-tree list is kept in bunOnly, so the authoritative Bun scope is preserved without silently inheriting the union's additional entries, while no discretionary further exclusions are granted (every recognized plan artifact outside that exact list is validated). The Bun rule-graph ids (validator/finding id planner_schema_validation, the catch-all rule id, the example canonical rule planner.user-system-flow.naming, and the parse prerequisite rule) are realization details kept in bunOnly; the core's verification states routing, the parse prerequisite, the never-scanned exception, and severity 3 / strict disposition generically. The word 'planner' is kept as the ATDD role name, not a stack reference. Instantiating the core with the Bun profile values plus the bunOnly items reproduces bun.json exactly: universal scope (all recognized artifacts, changed or not), the JSON Schema technology requirement, the routing-only attribution, the no-exemption parse prerequisite, the exactly-four-tree never-scanned exception, and strict enforcement are all preserved without weakening or strengthening.
